title: Manitoba Issues Fresh Round of Immigration Invitations as Province Hits 1,910 Skilled Worker Nominations in 2026
excerpt: The province's 13th PNP draw of the year targets employer-sponsored workers, francophone candidates, and regional community applicants through multiple pathways.
body:

  • Manitoba issued 77 immigration invitations on July 2, 2026, totaling 1,910 for the year.
  • Invitations targeted employer-sponsored workers, francophone candidates, and regional community applicants.
  • 15 of the latest invitations went to candidates with valid Express Entry profiles.
  • Manitoba's 13 draws in 2026 reflect a focus on addressing workforce shortages in key sectors.

Another Draw, Another Signal of Demand

Manitoba held its 274th Provincial Nominee Program draw on July 2, 2026, issuing 77 Letters of Advice to Apply under the Skilled Worker Stream. The draw brings the province's total invitations for 2026 to 1,910 — a steady pace that reflects Manitoba's continued appetite for immigrant talent to fill labor market gaps across key sectors.

> **"According to immigration data, India consistently ranks among the top source countries for Manitoba PNP nominations."**

"According to immigration data, India consistently ranks among the top source countries for Manitoba PNP nominations."

The invitations were distributed across four Strategic Recruitment Initiative pathways: 36 through Employer Services, 31 through the Temporary Public Policy to Facilitate Work Permits for Prospective PNP Candidates, 8 through the Francophone Community stream, and 2 through Regional Communities. The spread suggests Manitoba is casting a wide net, targeting both established employer-sponsored workers and candidates who can contribute to the province's francophone and rural communities.

What This Means for Indian Applicants

Canada's provincial nominee programs have become an increasingly important pathway for Indian immigrants, particularly as federal Express Entry draws have fluctuated in their targeting of specific occupations and NOC categories. Manitoba's PNP offers a more predictable route, especially for candidates already working in the province on temporary work permits or those who have graduated from Manitoba institutions.

The province has historically been welcoming to Indian newcomers. According to immigration data, India consistently ranks among the top source countries for Manitoba PNP nominations. The province's healthcare, manufacturing, and agricultural sectors have relied heavily on immigrant workers to address persistent labor shortages.

For candidates weighing their options between provinces, Manitoba's consistent draw schedule offers a degree of predictability that larger provinces like Ontario and British Columbia sometimes lack. The province has held 13 draws so far in 2026, averaging roughly two per month.

The Express Entry Advantage

Of the 77 invitations issued, 15 went to candidates who had declared valid Express Entry profiles and job seeker validation codes. When a provincial nominee also holds Express Entry eligibility, they receive an additional 600 Comprehensive Ranking System points — effectively guaranteeing an Invitation to Apply in the next federal draw. This dual-pathway approach can significantly accelerate the timeline from nomination to permanent residency.

Looking Ahead

Manitoba's immigration strategy continues to center on targeted recruitment aligned with labor market needs. The province's employer-driven model, where the majority of nominees come through established employment relationships, helps ensure that newcomers can integrate into the workforce quickly. For prospective applicants, maintaining an active Expression of Interest in Manitoba's system and building employment connections within the province remain the most effective strategies for securing a nomination.
